q1: SELECT DISTINCT VIEWER_ID AS ID FROM VIEWS GROUP BY VIEW_DATE, VIEWER_ID HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ARTICLE_ID) > 1 ORDER BY ID
q2: SELECT DISTINCT X.VIEWER_ID AS ID FROM ( SELECT V.VIEWER_ID, V.VIEW_DATE, COUNT(DISTINCT V.ARTICLE_ID) AS DISTINCT_VIEWS FROM VIEWS V GROUP BY 1,2 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT V.ARTICLE_ID) >1 ) AS X ORDER BY 1
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT DISTINCT VIEWER_ID AS ID FROM VIEWS GROUP BY VIEW_DATE, VIEWER_ID HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ARTICLE_ID) > 1 ORDER BY ID
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT DISTINCT X.VIEWER_ID AS ID FROM ( SELECT V.VIEWER_ID, V.VIEW_DATE, COUNT(DISTINCT V.ARTICLE_ID) AS DISTINCT_VIEWS FROM VIEWS V GROUP BY 1,2 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT V.ARTICLE_ID) >1 ) AS X ORDER BY 1
counterexample: INSERT INTO VIEWS (ARTICLE_ID, AUTHOR_ID, VIEWER_ID, VIEW_DATE) VALUES (1, 101, 201, '2023-01-01'); INSERT INTO VIEWS (ARTICLE_ID, AUTHOR_ID, VIEWER_ID, VIEW_DATE) VALUES (1, 101, 202, '2023-01-01');
explanation: Q1 groups by VIEW_DATE and VIEWER_ID, which means it considers the number of distinct articles viewed by each viewer on each specific date. Q2, on the other hand, groups by VIEWER_ID and VIEW_DATE, and it calculates the count of distinct articles for each viewer on each specific date, but it does not use the HAVING clause to filter viewers based on the count of distinct articles. This difference in the grouping and filtering conditions leads to different results.
counterexample_dsp: The test data should have at least two viewers, each viewing the same article on the same date, but the total count of distinct articles viewed by each viewer on that date should be different. This will cause Q1 and Q2 to return different results.
